author: 0.9.0_WK_IRPT_DASHBD~91
question: Does METHOD_ROWS row 3 (and the dim_return_method row emit_method_row writes for it) describe the Cottonwood rows, field by field; does a dim row 3 partition exist at the builder address.
denominator: emit_method_row writes 22 fields (account_return_daily.py lines 1897-1924); METHOD_ROWS row 3 carries 4 keys of its own (lines 119-124: valuation_source, value_basis, value_basis_ruling, fee_basis). 14 field groups below cover all 22 written fields plus valuation_source (23 of 23).

fields.field: valuation_source (METHOD_ROWS row 3; read by method_version_of against the entry, not written to the dim row)
fields.cottonwood_does: FWD-3 value is positions x as-traded close + cash leg; the entry declares valuation_source positions_x_as_traded_close, which is not custodian_reported, so method_version_of accepts row 3 for it.

fields.row3_states: TWR_DAILY_GEOMETRIC (constant, line 1898, inherited by every method row)
fields.cottonwood_does: FWD-3 return is ret_t = (value_t - flow_t) / value_(t-1) - 1, a daily return that the adapter links as TWR; same form as the producer's.

fields.row3_states: winner or END (line 1899); no caller passes a winner, so the written value is END (flows at end of day).
fields.cottonwood_does: FWD-3 flow timing defaults to end (module constant FLOW_TIMING, CLI default the same): ret_t = (value_t - flow_t) / value_(t-1) - 1, flows at end of day. The adapter takes the delivered return unchanged. The recorded run's command line is not in the repo; the code default is what is established.

fields.row3_states: cash_when_received (constant, line 1900, inherited from the row-2 path; METHOD_ROWS row 3 does not override it)
fields.cottonwood_does: FWD-3 does not separate income; it is inside the value through the cash leg. The cash ledger posts dv/dvlt/dvst at the file's PAY date (dividend_date default pay; the valuation run call at line 942 does not pass 'ex') and int as signed cash income, so a dividend or interest credit enters value when the cash posts, once (dvr posts -Amount against +Amount). That matches cash_when_received for cash-posted income. NOT ESTABLISHED FROM THE CODE: whether a bond's stored close carries accrued interest (a price-vendor property outside these files), and the exact flags of the 107,316-row run (not recorded in the repo). The adapter's income_received and income_return columns are NULL by design; that is a column statement, not the basis.

fields.row3_states: POSITIONS-BASED EQUITY = account value rebuilt from positions at the entry's declared price_basis, plus the entry's declared cash
fields.cottonwood_does: value = positions x as-traded close + cash leg (method_r28 ledger); the entry declares price_basis as_traded.

fields.row3_states: 1.0.0_SA_CTO~DELL2 ADDENDUM 13.2 (msg 3501): a positions-based channel names its own method row, never 2
fields.cottonwood_does: The entry names method_version 3 itself; the adapter stamps it through method_version_of(entry). A citation, not a computation.
Fees are a drag inside the return (a fee is not a flow), so the return is after fees; the entry field fee_treatment carries it as net_of_fees. The adapter's fee_amount is NULL with FEE_RAIL_UNUSED.

fields.row3_states: Values copied from a thresholds file passed at write time (lines 1904-1913); row 3 states none of its own.
fields.cottonwood_does: The adapter runs with thresholds=None (no measured thresholds exist for this firm) and every row is GUARD_NOT_REACHED, so the guard never graded a Cottonwood row. emit_method_row indexes thresholds[...] and would refuse None; a row 3 written for Cottonwood would carry numbers measured on another population. No entry field carries them (the entry has only the three method fields). Whether that is acceptable is the CTO's; nothing in row 3's own text is untrue of the rows.

fields.row3_states: WITHDRAWN (PRD v0.4 ruling 17): a guard disagreement serves no number; HOLDINGS_INCOME_FALLBACK is never emitted.
fields.cottonwood_does: The adapter refuses HOLDINGS_INCOME_FALLBACK and emits only TWR or NOT_MEASURABLE.
The daily return uses no day-count; nothing in the Cottonwood path reads or contradicts it. Not establishable from the code either way.

fields.row3_states: tieout is a run argument (line 1917); tieout_tolerance 0.0035 under batch 181 (lines 259-260).
fields.cottonwood_does: The adapter makes no vendor tie-out and cites none; it is a producer constant carried on any row written.
The adapter states the same label in its manifest text.
Provenance of the write; the adapter takes SCHEMA_VERSION from the producer. Not a claim about the method.
The entry's registry_key z09 resolves to the firm cottonwood, the scope the adapter writes under.
The entry names 3; the adapter stamps mv_entry on every row and manifest.

verdict_basis: No field reads FALSE. Four groups are NOT_STATED (fee_basis, which the entry's fee_treatment carries; the guard thresholds, which no entry field carries and the adapter never supplies; day_count; tie-out and provenance fields).
open_items: Income basis: cash-posted income (dv, dvlt, dvst, int) enters value on the file's pay date; whether a bond's stored close carries accrued interest is not in these files, and the exact flags of the 107,316-row run are not recorded in the repo (code defaults used).

No dim row 3 partition exists: writing it needs --thresholds-in (the row cannot be written without measured thresholds, line 2031), and the Cottonwood firm has no measured thresholds (adapter runs thresholds=None). Which thresholds a Cottonwood row 3 should carry is not decided by this record.

read.result: rc=254 An error occurred (404) when calling the HeadObject operation: Not Found. A 404 from a bucket whose control read on the same shim succeeded; emit_method_row writes manifest.json and data.parquet together (lines 1927-1935 region), so a missing manifest means no partition.
rc=0, object present (ContentLength and LastModified returned)

read_history: Before these two reads, four reads used a mis-built address (registry key z09 / 08335338 in the firm slot instead of the firm token the producer's firm_scope returns): one s3 ls pair and one head-object pair, all not-found, including the control, which is how the mis-build was seen. They are not used as evidence. See the surprise row.
